exact_source_lessons: Historical Mnemosyne used MD5 snapshots and a stability-index/Hot-Start concept; modern restoration keeps the hint but forbids skipping security/integrity gates.
Historical ModuleIntegrator dynamically imported files and fell back to discovery order on dependency cycles; modern restoration is static and fail-closed.
Historical MonkeyPatcher patch transforms were mostly stubs and its evaluator executed module.update()/reload; modern restoration preserves evidence/history intent but not actuator authority.
Historical Auditor could miss syntax-valid import-time failures such as a bare top-level `python` identifier; modern static audit explicitly catches that failure class.
Historical Hypnos could consume and delete a shared dreams.json bus while Rex understood only one schema dialect; modern router is non-destructive and preserves observed_type.
Historical Yaks Skeleton contained a useful five-phase policy backbone but its activation hooks were not a proven capability controller; modern version is declarative only.
Historical HRain daemon was an asynchronous transport organ, distinct from recovery/liveness daemon; modern restoration separates durable event production from network transport authority.
Ghost Rider proves registry labels can contradict executable behavior; exact bytes therefore outrank registry semantics.
permanent_laws: CYCLE -> HOLD; NEVER FALL BACK TO DISCOVERY ORDER
